transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-05 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Flynn (Redwood SE), Dana Rivers (Helios Procurement), Liam O'Connor (Helios Security), Priya Menon (Helios Legal), Ethan Park (Helios Platform)

Summary:
High-level intake handoff between Redwood AE/SE and Helios procurement/legal/security. Main topics: MSA/DPA redline expectations, SLA targets (p99 latency goals), deployment options (hosted vs private VPC), KMS/HSM and audit log requirements, pricing approval path and procurement timeline. Agreed to send MSA redline summary + schedule technical deep dive next week.

Topics: MSA redlines; DPA & data retention; SLA targets and credits; VPC/private deployment constraints; SSO/SAML and SCIM; KMS integration; procurement timeline and PO process.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone thanks for joining today, uh this is Aisha from Redwood, I think we have Marcus joining for the technical bits. Hi all.
[00:07] Dana: Hi Aisha, thanks. We wanted to do an intake handoff — procurement asked us to get the commercial and security asks captured so legal can triage.
[00:15] Marcus: Morning — or afternoon — yes, Marcus here, I'll cover hosting options and what changes with Dedicated vs Private.
[00:22] Priya: Priya from legal, hi. We'll be focusing on MSA/DPA redlines, specifically data residency and audit language.
[00:27] Liam: Liam, security — we'll mostly look at encryption in transit, KMS, SOC2 and the audit logs.
[00:31] Ethan: Ethan - platform - quick note, we have high throughput endpoints for batch scoring and latency-sensitive real-time features.

[00:45] Aisha: Great. Quick context: Helios is evaluating Redwood for model serving across two products — inference for recommendations and an internal embeddings pipeline. The procurement timeline is about six weeks if legal and security are happy. Wanted to align on what you need from us.
[00:58] Dana: Procurement side, just to be explicit: we need a standard PO flow, invoice terms, cancellation terms for pilot, and pricing approval path. We'll escalate to our Sourcing committee if the delta to our procurement template is material.
[01:12] Aisha: Understood. We'll include commercial terms and a sample invoice flow in the package. On the pricing side, we surfaced two pricing models earlier — hosted pay-as-you-go and a committed Dedicated capacity quote. Which is the procurement preference?
[01:26] Ethan: We prefer predictable spend, so Dedicated looks more likely but we want the option to failover to hosted in case of spike or if capacity issues occur. That implies a SLO for cross-option fallback.
[01:38] Marcus: Right, for Dedicated we provide reserved GPU pools; for failover we can route to hosted variants but there are latency/cost tradeoffs. We can add a routing fallback policy but need to agree on SLA tiers for each.
[01:49] Priya: On the MSA / DPA — our legal team flagged three primary concerns: data residency (can't leave the EU for certain PII), audit access to logs for compliance, and stronger indemnity language around data breaches.
[02:02] Aisha: Noted. Redwood can offer a Private deployment (VPC) option where data does not transit public nets and we support EU region deployments, plus integrations with customer KMS. For indemnity we'll need to review specifics. We have standard language but it's usually negotiable for enterprise.
[02:16] Liam: For security, two asks: 1) evidence of SOC2 Type II and recent cert, 2) ability to push audit logs to our SIEM or provide an export. Also need support for customer-managed KMS and HSMs.
[02:30] Marcus: We have SOC2 Type II and can provide the report under NDA; for logs we support streaming audit events to a customer endpoint or S3; and KMS integration is supported for Private — hosted also has KMS options but customer-managed is restricted to Private or dedicated with a customer-side KMS proxy.
[02:46] Ethan: On SLA — we need p99 tail latency targets for the real-time endpoint, and an availability SLA for Dedicated pools. Typical internal bar is p99 < 200ms for 512 token context for the recommendation endpoint. Is that realistic?
[02:59] Marcus: We can get close on lighter models; larger LLMs will be higher. Our published latency profiles list p99 for the curated recommendation model at ~180-220ms on Dedicated with n1 GPUs, but exact numbers depend on sequence length and model variant. We can run a short benchmark using a representative prompt set.
[03:19] Priya: If benchmarks show higher tails we may ask for service credits or a defined remediation plan.
[03:25] Aisha: That's fair — we usually propose SLA credits for availability and a remediation plan for prolonged degradations; credits vary by commitment. We'll draft an SLA appendix showing tiers and proposed credits.
[03:36] Dana: Procurement will need billing cadence and how overage is handled. For Dedicated, are commitments monthly or annual? Also escalation path to open a support ticket that triggers an on-call SE?
[03:47] Aisha: Dedicated supports monthly and annual commitments; we can include an option for monthly reserved capacity with a short-term ramp. Support tiers: standard includes email and ticketing; premium adds an on-call SE rotation and faster response times. We'll map that in the proposal.
[03:58] Liam: On the technical side, if we go Private, what's the network architecture? Do you require VPN, direct connect, or can you support peering? Also how are keys rotated?
[04:09] Marcus: For Private we support VPC peering and AWS Direct Connect options; VPN is possible for smaller bands. KMS key rotation follows the customer's policy if customer-managed keys are used; otherwise Redwood rotates keys but we can provide rotation logs.
[04:23] Ethan: We also need the ability to pin model versions per environment and run canary rollouts. Can Redwood provide model pinning and A/B routing?
[04:31] Marcus: Yes, model versioning and canary/A-B rollout tools exist in the Console. We can set traffic splits and automatic fallback to a previous version if error rates spike. That will be included in the configuration appendix.
[04:43] Priya: One more legal note: data retention windows — for Helios' regulated dataset we need deletion guarantees after 90 days, plus forensic export on demand. Is that supported?
[04:54] Aisha: We support configurable retention windows and can add contract language for deletion and export within a defined SLA; for forensic exports we'll outline process and time-to-deliver in the DPA.
[05:05] Dana: On procurement cadence — if we get the redline and SLA appendix this week, procurement can route to Sourcing committee next Tuesday and then legal will follow; target signing window end of February.
[05:16] Aisha: Sounds good. We'll push a focused package: 1) MSA with redline summary, 2) DPA with retention/export language, 3) SLA appendix with proposed p99 targets and credits, and 4) commercial term sheet showing Dedicated vs hosted pricing.
[05:29] Liam: For the security onboarding we want a one-hour technical session where Marcus walks through network, logging, and KMS flows.
[05:35] Marcus: Happy to do that. I'll prepare a short runbook and sample benchmark steps.
[05:40] Priya: We'll probably have a couple of must-have legal clauses — data residency, indemnity cap adjustments, and a narrow security exception for subcontractors — we'll send those over.
[05:50] Aisha: Quick question on procurement process — Dana, do you need a certified PO template or a sandbox invoice to run in your AP system?
[05:58] Dana: A sandbox invoice is helpful; also we need documentation for tax and remittance addresses.
[06:03] Aisha: We'll include a sample invoice and remittance details in the packet.
[06:09] Ethan: Regarding pricing approvals: who signs off on the final commercial? Is it procurement, finance, or an exec sponsor?
[06:15] Dana: Procurement will push to finance for approvals over $250k ARR; for smaller deals our procurement + platform can sign. We expect the initial pilot commitment will be under that threshold.
[06:26] Aisha: Good to know. We'll size the pilot to stay under the $250k mark and then show dedicated commit options for scaling.
[06:34] Marcus: Quick note on metrics — if you can share top-traffic routes and approximate RPS we can size the Dedicated pool and give a more precise cost estimate.
[06:43] Ethan: I'll compile a list and send it.
[06:46] Priya: One procedural question: will Redwood accept redlines via DocuSign comments or do you prefer a redline PDF?
[06:53] Aisha: Either works; we prefer tracked redlines in Word for legal review and a short 'difference' summary. We'll deliver both if needed.
[07:03] Dana: Okay next steps we'll expect your packet by Friday and we'll route internally.
[07:08] Aisha: Recap: Aisha sends MSA+DPA+SLA+commercial by 2026-02-07; Marcus schedules technical deep-dive and benchmark plan for the week of 2026-02-16; Helios sends legal non-negotiables and traffic list by 2026-02-12.
[07:22] Marcus: Thanks everyone, look forward to the deep dive.
[07:25] Liam: Thanks.
[07:27] Priya: Thanks all, bye.

End of transcript. Notes: occasional transcription errors in names and product terms observed; this recording captured some overlapping talk when legal and procurement were discussing the escalation path.
